text:
A: Hiya! Hello, can you hear me okay?
B: Yes. Hi. Tomasz.
A: Daniel, nice to meet you. I'm in Newark, East Midlands. Where are you, sorry?
B: Walthamstow. East London.
A: Oh, London, nice. So, er, I'm a director at a lettings firm, family business, my dad started it. About a hundred and forty properties round Newark. What do you do?
B: Electrician. Domestic mostly. The lady before, Nicola, she said you do lettings. She said you could give me work.
A: Did she? Ha, that's nice of her. Yeah, no, definitely. What sort of stuff?
B: A lot of EICRs for landlords. Testing. And consumer units, rewires, EV chargers.
A: Oh, EICRs, we live and die by them. Every five years for every property, and I've got them all on a spreadsheet, colour-coded, red when it's due in sixty days. Honestly, half my job is chasing contractors to get them done before they run out.
B: That's good, the spreadsheet. Most landlords call the week before. Then it's a problem.
A: Exactly, and then it's my problem, cos the landlord rings me. Is it busy, London, for that?
B: Very busy. Lots of flats, lots of old wiring. Sometimes the previous electrician left a mess. No labels, wires everywhere in the consumer unit. Then it takes twice as long.
A: That must do your head in.
B: Yeah. I label every circuit. It's the first thing I check, if someone was careful or not.
A: Oh, I'd love you, then. We had one last year, a contractor, he signed off a flat and two weeks later the tenant's ringing me cos half the sockets don't work. I were on the phone to her for an hour calming her down. She was really upset, she had a little one.
B: That's not right. You test it, you write what you find. Simple.
A: Yeah. Are you employed, or self-employed?
B: Employed now. Small contractor. In two years I want to go on my own. I'm saving first, six months of money.
A: That's sensible, yeah. My dad always says have a buffer. Do you live with anyone, in London?
B: My partner. Hannah.
A: No way, my girlfriend's called Hannah!
B: Okay. Common name, I think.
A: Ha, yeah, true. What does yours do?
B: Dental nurse. In Leytonstone.
A: Mine's a primary school teacher, in Grantham. She did a nativity last Christmas and I went to watch, and honestly, I got a bit emotional, which I didn't expect. Kids in tea towels.
B: Tea towels?
A: Sorry, on their heads, for the shepherds. It's a British thing, I think.
B: Ah, okay. In Poland it's more church, the nativity.
A: Oh right. Are you from Poland, then?
B: Yes, Lublin. Thirteen years here.
A: Do you get back much?
B: Twice a year. Christmas and summer. I book early from Luton, it's cheap.
